subject: [RFC PATCH v3 0/8] batch lookups in follow_page_mask()

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: reviewer expressed strong disagreement with the addition of new functions using outdated 'follow_page_*' terminology and suggested avoiding such additions
reviews.raw_body:
I'll try getting to this soon. As I raised previously, the whole follow_page_*
terminology is just stale, and likely we should just not add new functions that
use this terminology.

I.e., follow_page_pte_commit()

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David expressed concerns that the function name and abstraction in follow_page_pte_commit() are not clear, suggesting it may be better named to reflect its purpose of grabbing a folio reference. He also proposed simplifying the helper by removing unnecessary code and special-casing ptes.
reviews.raw_body:
If a function needs 4 lines of internal doc to understand what it does, then
maybe it's not the right function name or abstraction. :)

I don't particularly enjoy the "commit" terminology, it looses the detail of the
most important thing this function is supposed to to: grab a folio reference.

We're passing in the pte only to do a single pte_dirty(). If the helper is
actually what we want, likely we just just pass in the pte_dirty() directly and
remove all pte leftovers from the helper.

I'd assume that we'd want a function where we can similarly punch in a PMD/PUD
and have it do the same thing as well, instead of special-casing ptes.

Let me think about this some more, I might have to play with the code myself to
understand how this should all be cleaned up.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author noticed that the pmd and pud code don't call mark_folio_dirty() like the pte code does, which is a problem for huge folios from filesystems; author agrees to add this functionality.
reviews.raw_body:
Looking at the differences between the pte and pmd
code, there is another big thing that stands out.

The pte code will call mark_folio_dirty() when
needed, but the pmd and pud code do not.

For hugetlbfs we can get away with that, but for
huge folios coming from a filesystem, don't we
want to call mark_folio_dirty() somewhere?

I'm happy to do whatever cleanups we can do to
this code while we're here.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David questioned the purpose of gup_grab_and_store_folio_pages() and was uncertain about its functionality.

Reviewer David noted an inconsistency in the use of a helper function across different places in follow_page_mask(), expressing concern that it may not be a bug but rather a design issue.
reviews.raw_body:
It does more than grabbing, hm, let me think.

gup_grab_and_store_folio_pages()

not sure.

---

Yes, and my gut feeling is that the same helper should be also used in the other
places. Maybe there is no real bug there, but the inconsistency is concerning.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledges that moving gup_fill_pages() call outside the lock is necessary for PUD path, but notes it would leave only page grabbing and marking operations inside the lock.

The author acknowledges that marking a folio dirty is necessary for data integrity, but notes that not marking it dirty could affect dirty balancing.
reviews.raw_body:
It does more than grabbing, but if we want to
have the PUD path use this same function, we
will probably want to move the gup_fill_pages()
call to outside the lock.

At that point we'll be left with grabbing the
pages, and marking the folio dirty/accessed,
plus the arch_make_folio_accessible() call,
which seems to be a noop on anything but s390,
where it makes the page accessible to the
hypervisor (not sure when/why GUP needs this).

---

The page table dirty bits should ensure that we
don't lose any data written to the page, but not
marking the folio dirty might mess with dirty
balancing.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-08-12.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of follow_page_mask() by allowing it to batch lookups and reduce lock contention. The current implementation walks the page tables one page at a time, even when contiguous pages are requested. This series changes follow_page_mask() to return a count and an array of pages, instead of a single struct page, enabling more efficient handling of large folios. Patches 1-4 prepare for this change by refactoring and splitting existing functions. Patch 5 optimizes huge page paths, patch 6 simplifies the handling of subpages, and patches 7 and 8 implement batched lookups and refcount batching, respectively. The series includes benchmark results showing a significant performance improvement.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is addressing David's concern about sub-folio dirty tracking for filesystem-backed large folios and get_user_pages(). The author questions whether marking a folio dirty at GUP time is necessary, pointing out that __access_remote_vm() already does this. They suggest fixing places in the kernel where pages are not marked dirty after writing with FOLL_WRITE.
reviews.raw_body:
Heh, now the filesystem people want sub-folio dirty
tracking, to reduce write amplification.

https://lore.kernel.org/all/aocFPRgqieScf_yo@pedro-suse.lan/

This makes me wonder that while your suggestion
makes sense for anonymous and tmpfs memory, we might
need something else for filesystem backed large
folios and get_user_pages?

Thinking about it some more, we are marking the 
folio dirty before (potentially long before) a write
is actually done.

Doesn't that give the flushing code time to clean
the page (by writing out content identical to what
is already on disk) before the actual dirtying of
the memory, through e.g. PTRACE_POKE is done?

Does the dirtying of folios and/or pages need to
be done when they are actually being written to,
and not at GUP time?

It looks like __access_remote_vm() already does
that dirtying, as do most of the other places
that use GUP with FOLL_WRITE.

A number of places use unpin_user_pages_dirty(_lock)
to get the pages marked dirty at unpin time, after
the data has been written into the pages.

However, there seem to be some places in the
kernel that are not marking pages dirty when
they write after GUP with FOLL_WRITE.

I suppose we need to fix those, given how
sometimes they can pin pages for a long time,
and do multiple writes over a long period of
time?

I'm combing through the tree now to find those
places.

This raises the question whether we want to
call mark_folio_dirty() at all from inside
GUP.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: John Hubbard
reviews.summary: Reviewer John Hubbard noted that GUP should not set folios or pages dirty, as this typically requires filesystem-coordinated steps and can lead to problems if the page is unexpectedly dirty.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Rik,

You have delved too deep, and now uncovered something that's been
a problem for the whole time. :)

Specifically, "no, GUP should not be setting folios nor pages
dirty", because that generally needs to be done as part of a filesystem
coordinated set of steps. If the page is dirty, and the filesystem
didn't expect it to be, that leads to problems.

This is part of the big, remaining set of required fixes, that
launched the creation of pin_user_pages*() and related. Connecting
up the filesystems properly is yet to be done. And until then, this
is a real defect.

thanks,
-- 
John Hubbard

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about drivers failing to mark pages dirty after writing to them, and has agreed to create patches to fix this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Not just filesystems.

I found about two dozen places where drivers
fail to mark a page dirty after writing to
it, after obtaining the page from GUP.

I'll get out patches for that, unless there's
some reason I shouldn't.

--

reviews.author: John Hubbard
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that marking a page dirty in follow_page_mask() can lead to issues if not coordinated with the filesystem, and agreed that this is one of several problems

Reviewer noted that ext4_page_mkwrite() and other drivers cannot run set_page_dirty() on a file-backed page because it requires preparation steps like sb_start_pagefault(), file_update_time(), and filemap_invalidate_lock_shared() to be executed before folio_mark_dirty(). The reviewer suggested that the filesystem needs a way to be told before the device writes, which is where lease proposals come in.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, I agree about that problem, but it's not the only one. It turns
out that the only thing worse than failing to mark a page dirty is
marking it dirty without coordinating with the filesystem.

---

Well...on a file-backed page, marking it dirty is the *last* step of
a sequence, and a driver cannot run the earlier steps.

ext4_page_mkwrite() into ext4_block_page_mkwrite() runs it in this
order:

	sb_start_pagefault(inode->i_sb);	/* freeze protection */
	file_update_time(vma->vm_file);
	filemap_invalidate_lock_shared(mapping);	/* truncate */
	ext4_journal_start(inode, EXT4_HT_WRITE_PAGE, credits);
	ext4_block_write_begin(handle, folio, 0, len, get_block);
	folio_mark_dirty(folio);
	ext4_journal_stop(handle);
	folio_wait_stable(folio);

A set_page_dirty() at the driver's write site is that
folio_mark_dirty(), but with none of the preparation above it.

ext4 documents this case already, in ext4_journalled_dirty_folio() on
the data=journal path:

  * ... except for the case when someone
  * had the page pinned and dirtied the page through this pin (e.g. by doing
  * direct IO to it). In that case we'd need to attach buffers here to the
  * transaction but we cannot due to lock ordering.

Its workaround is folio_set_checked(), which defers the real work to
ext4_writepages(). If ext4 can't do the preparation from inside the
dirty call, a driver can't either.

So for a file-backed page there's nothing the driver can add. What's
missing is a way for the filesystem to be told before the device
writes, and to revoke the pin when it needs to, which is where the
lease proposals come in. None of that exists today.

And yes, unpin_user_pages_dirty_lock() is in the same awkward mess.

thanks,
-- 
John Hubbard

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledges that there is an issue with FOLL_WRITE folios not setting their dirty bits after writing, but is unsure how to improve the situation without extensive filesystem changes.
reviews.raw_body:
That still leaves the question on what to do with
code paths that rely on get_user_pages(FOLL_WRITE)
to set the dirty bit on pages, and then do not set
the dirty bit themselves after they write the page.

Would it be better to move the dirty bit setting
till after the write (to the page) has happened,
even if that code does not queue up a filesystem
write?

Does unpin_user_pages_dirty_lock() need to call
Folio_set_checked() ?

You've made it pretty clear what is wrong, but
I'm confused as to how we could improve the situation,
at least without waiting for extensive filesystem
changes first.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.
